methods.title: ReWeaver: Towards Simulation-Ready and Topology-Accurate Garment Reconstruction
methods.evidence: The paper reconstructs panels, seams and connectivity in 2D UV and 3D from as few as four RGB views, targeting simulation-ready garments.
implementationImplications: Represent image-derived garments as explicit panels and seam connectivity before final meshing.
Persist both 2D pattern-space and 3D garment-space correspondence when reconstruction is used.
Reject visually similar but unstructured shells as the canonical source when panel topology is recoverable.
rejectionCriteria: No traceable panel or seam model for an image-reconstructed garment.
Topology cannot support controlled edits or simulation-oriented validation.

methods.title: AutoSew: A Geometric Approach to Stitching Prediction with Graph Neural Networks
methods.evidence: The paper predicts stitch correspondences directly from 2D contours with graph matching and differentiable optimal transport, including multi-edge connections.
implementationImplications: Store seam pairing as a graph instead of relying on object names or manual adjacency alone.
Validate edge-length compatibility, orientation and multi-edge connectivity before cloth assembly.
Keep manual stitching as an auditable fallback until the learned predictor is licensed and reproduced.
rejectionCriteria: Unpaired or ambiguous pattern edges remain in a release candidate.
Stitch topology changes without an explicit connectivity diff.

methods.title: ExMesh: EXplicit Mesh Reconstruction with Topology Adaptation
methods.evidence: The paper combines explicit mesh optimization with adaptive splitting and merging while maintaining UV coordinates.
implementationImplications: Any topology refinement must preserve UV continuity and material alignment.
Record vertex and face count changes and reject new degenerate or fragmented geometry.
Prefer coarse-to-fine refinement over uniformly dense generation.
rejectionCriteria: Topology edits create degenerate faces, UV discontinuity or unnecessary density.
High detail is produced only by uncontrolled subdivision.

methods.title: DAMA: Disentangled Body-Anchored Gaussians for Controllable Multi-Layered Avatars
methods.evidence: The paper explicitly models garment separation, stacking order, penetration rate and penetration depth for multi-layer avatars.
implementationImplications: Declare layer order and body anchoring for every garment component.
Measure penetration count and depth, not only render appearance.
Keep body-conforming layers separate from outer loose layers.
rejectionCriteria: Layer order is implicit or inconsistent across poses.
Critical body or inter-garment penetration remains unresolved.

methods.title: NI-Tex: Non-isometric Image-based Garment Texture Generation
methods.evidence: The paper generates spatially aligned PBR materials from non-isometric image and geometry pairs and uses uncertainty-guided multi-view baking.
implementationImplications: Generate or author PBR channels separately from geometry.
Bake from multiple views and prioritize uncertain or occluded regions in later passes.
Evaluate seam continuity, cross-view color consistency and material response.
rejectionCriteria: A single projected image is treated as production-ready texture.
Visible seams, cross-view color drift or material-channel mismatch remain.

methods.title: NaTex: Seamless Texture Generation as Latent Color Diffusion
methods.evidence: The paper generates texture color directly in 3D to address occlusion, boundary alignment and cross-view consistency limitations of multi-view baking.
implementationImplications: Benchmark texture seams and occluded regions against a 3D-consistent representation.
Do not accept multi-view texture baking when hidden regions are unreviewed.
rejectionCriteria: Occluded texture regions are filled without evidence or review.
Boundary alignment fails at UV islands or garment edges.

methods.title: PhySkin: Physics-based Bone-driven Neural Garment Simulation
methods.evidence: The preprint uses reduced-space bone handles and self-supervised physics objectives for fast garment draping with gravity, stretch, bending and collision avoidance.
implementationImplications: Treat bone handles as a reduced deformation space rather than assigning arbitrary weights only.
Separate offline physics fitting from runtime handle evaluation.
Benchmark loose garments across body shapes and required poses before runtime adoption.
rejectionCriteria: Loose garments rely only on static linear blend skinning without deformation evidence.
Runtime claims are made without measured cost and pose/body generalization tests.

methods.title: UNIC: Neural Garment Deformation Field for Real-time Clothed Character Animation
methods.evidence: The preprint learns an instance-specific continuous deformation field for complex garment topology and new motion sequences.
implementationImplications: Use per-garment deformation evaluation when topology is complex.
Benchmark continuous-field deformation against bone-driven and physics baselines.
Do not require one model to generalize across unrelated garments.
rejectionCriteria: A deformation method is selected without a garment-specific benchmark.
Real-time suitability is assumed without target-device measurement.

methods.title: Human Geometry Distribution for 3D Animation Generation
methods.evidence: The paper evaluates high-fidelity human geometry animation with detailed clothing dynamics and reports both geometric metrics and a perceptual user study.
implementationImplications: Evaluate deformation with both geometric error and perceptual review.
Test short transitions and long motion consistency instead of isolated poses only.
Preserve garment identity and fine detail across animation.
rejectionCriteria: Only static poses are used to claim dynamic garment quality.
Temporal flicker or identity drift is not reviewed.

structured-patterns: Image-derived garments must have an explicit panel model or an auditable reason for a non-panel construction.
The editable source must preserve the relationship between design references, panels and the final mesh.
stitch-assembly: Seam connectivity must be stored explicitly and checked for unmatched, reversed or incompatible edges.
Assembly changes require a connectivity diff and regenerated pose evidence.
topology-uv: Topology changes must preserve UV continuity, face orientation and material assignment.
Degenerate faces, fragmented shells and uncontrolled density are release blockers.
layering-collision: Every component must declare its body or garment layer and intended clearance.
Penetration must be measured across required poses, including depth or severity, not only counted visually.
pbr-texture: Textures must be reviewed across all required views with separate material channels where applicable.
Seams, occluded regions and cross-view color/material consistency must be explicitly inspected.
runtime-deformation: Tight and loose garments must use different deformation strategies where needed.
Loose garments require a measured bone-handle, physics or neural deformation benchmark before runtime claims.
dynamic-evaluation: Required static poses are necessary but not sufficient for loose or layered garments.
A motion sequence must be reviewed for temporal consistency, collision, detail retention and customer-visible artifacts.
